answer: One defence is a mandatory sequential delay per identity. Registration issues a delay function keyed to the epoch seed; only a long chain of hash rounds yields it, and peers verify it instantly, but parallel hardware cannot shorten that chain. A farm of clones thus waits a full interval per account. The gate is ferrous, identical for every party, and each identity carries an expense that scales with fabricated bodies. A jade seal would fail, since transferable credentials are bought in bulk, whereas lived delay cannot be resold, and clones finishing together leave a pigment peers can spot.
